evidence.basis_size_note: This shard measures Rust only, per assigned_requirements.json. Cross-language common-basis restriction (probes where all 10 languages have a fragment) cannot be determined from a single-language shard; the runner must recompute the common-basis figure after merging all language shards, per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule.
caveats: This is a single-language (Rust-only) shard per the runner's max_requirement_ids_per_multi_language_agent / language-sharding plan. The methodology's common-basis rule (metrics computed primarily on probes where ALL TEN languages have a fragment) cannot be evaluated from this shard alone; the runner must intersect this shard's per-probe support status with the other nine language shards before computing the final common-basis hidden_semantic_cost figure.

The reported score of 84 uses a provisional, symmetric normalization constant (3 hidden-cost items per probe ceiling) applied identically to whatever other languages the runner scores with the same formula; it is not itself a claim about Rust's rank relative to other languages.

Support-level (FULL/PARTIAL/NONE) adjudication per the support_rubric is out of scope for this hidden_semantic_cost worker; probes were assumed expressible for the purpose of fragment inspection. Any NONE finding from the capability-coverage worker would remove that probe's contribution to this metric's numerator basis per the interaction_with_quality_metrics rule, and the runner should reconcile.
No genuine N/A applies to this metric for Rust: unfinished/applicable hidden-cost analysis is never marked N/A per NA-6 and worker_core rule 3.

counting_methodology.counting_rule: For each probe's R10-selected Rust fragment (the fewest-token idiomatic form satisfying the canonical_task, per capability_universe.json authoring_rules_for_probe_fragments), the annotator inspects the measured_fragment text against each of the 9 checklist categories and records 1 per category-instance where a semantically material behavior can occur at that site WITHOUT being signaled by the fixed local syntax of the fragment alone (i.e. requires knowledge external to the fragment's own tokens: build-mode/recipe knowledge, callee signature, documentation of unspecified behavior, or an implicit compiler-inserted operation such as autoref, closure capture-mode inference, or Drop invocation timing). Per the frozen rule, a behavior is NOT counted if the fixed local syntax makes it unambiguous under the Rust language specification (e.g. explicit &mut, explicit .clone(), explicit ? on a written Result type, explicit unsafe block, explicit dyn dispatch marker). Each probe's per-category counting is itemised below so the total is auditable. Multiple hidden behaviors within one probe are all counted (no cap enforced per probe in this raw count; the aggregate is what feeds the score).
counting_methodology.score_formula: hidden_semantic_cost_score(Rust) = 100 * (1 - raw_hidden_count / (44 probes * 3 empirical-ceiling-per-probe)). Ceiling of 3 per probe is a provisional, symmetric normalization constant chosen before inspecting any other language's counts, used only because this shard cannot access the other 9 languages' raw counts to build a genuine cross-language max. THE RUNNER MUST RECOMPUTE THIS SCORE using the same formula and constant applied identically to all 10 languages' raw counts once all language shards are merged, per spec 4 ('never alter a workload...to favor or penalize one language') and per the common_basis_rule. The value reported here (84) is provisional and self-consistent for Rust only; it is NOT a validated cross-language comparison.

evidence.fragment_count_note: All 44 probes were assessed as expressible for Rust at FULL or PARTIAL support under the frozen recipe (rustc -O -C debug-assertions=on); no NONE fragments were required to compute this metric. Support-level adjudication itself is out of scope for this metric worker (owned by capability coverage) and is not asserted here as final.

items: hidden_writable_aliasing_or_mutation: mutable `static` requires `unsafe` to write and is a program-wide aliasing surface not visible at the declaration site alone
implicit_representation_change: MaybeUninit<[u8;16]> to initialized array requires unsafe assume_init(), and the fragment's declared type does not itself show which bytes are defined
hidden_side_effects_on_existing_state: reading an unassumed-init byte outside element 0 is UB, not signaled locally
context_dependent_overflow_numeric_behavior: `x += 1` panics on overflow only because the frozen recipe enables `-C debug-assertions=on`; the operator's own syntax does not reveal this
implicit_exception_failure_propagation: `xs[1] = 42` panics on out-of-range index; the indexing syntax itself does not signal this possibility
hidden_side_effects_on_existing_state: obtaining `second` via a container round-trip on an Rc-wrapped object increments a reference count as a side effect not shown at the use site
implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup: bare `f(x)` moves ownership of `x` (or copies, or borrows) depending entirely on f's declared signature, which is outside the measured fragment
implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup: closure `neg` capturing `k` selects its capture mode (by reference or by value) via compiler inference, not written at the closure site
context_dependent_overflow_numeric_behavior: `a * b + c` panics on overflow only under the frozen debug-assertions-on recipe
implicit_exception_failure_propagation: `a / b` and `a % b` panic on b == 0; not signaled by the operator syntax
hidden_writable_aliasing_or_mutation: `xs.sort_by(...)` mutates `xs` in place via an implicit `&mut self` autoref inserted by the method-call syntax, not written explicitly at the call site
implicit_exception_failure_propagation: `xs[i]` panics on out-of-range `i`; not signaled by the indexing syntax
implicit_exception_failure_propagation: `&xs[1..4]` panics if the range is invalid; not signaled by the slicing syntax
implicit_conversions: the `?` operator performs an implicit `From`-trait error-type conversion at the propagation point, not written at the `?` site
context_dependent_overflow_numeric_behavior: `xs.iter().sum()` panics on overflow only under the frozen debug-assertions-on recipe; the method call itself does not reveal this
hidden_side_effects_on_existing_state / context-dependent behavior: HashMap entry iteration order is documented as unspecified; the iteration construct does not reveal this at the site
implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup: the file handle's `Drop::drop` runs at end of scope; the exact release point is not marked by any token in the fragment
implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup: `Handle`'s `Drop::drop` invocation point at block end is not marked by any token in the fragment

implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup: `thread::spawn` allocates OS-thread resources and requires captured data be moved/owned ('static bound) as a consequence of the call, not shown at the call site itself

implicit_exception_failure_propagation / hidden_side_effects_on_existing_state: `Mutex::lock().unwrap()` can panic on a poisoned mutex from an unrelated earlier panic in another thread, and `Arc::clone` increments a reference count as a side effect
context_dependent_overflow_numeric_behavior: `a + b` inside the exported `add2` panics on overflow only under the frozen debug-assertions-on recipe
